name: Calendar
description: Date, month and year grids with single, range and multi selection, roving-tabindex keyboard navigation and per-day semantic dates; the selection value types live in the date_math primitive.

fields.cellBackground: StateValue<ThemedColor>? - per-state fill of an unselected cell; rest = transparent, hovered = accent
fields.cellForeground: StateValue<ThemedColor>? - per-state label colour; null = foreground
fields.todayBackground: ThemedColor? - fill of today's cell; null = secondary
fields.selectedBackground: ThemedColor? - fill of a selected cell; null = primary
fields.selectedForeground: ThemedColor? - label of a selected cell; null = primaryForeground
fields.rangeBackground: ThemedColor? - fill inside a range; null = secondary
fields.cellWidth: double? - 32 for days, 56 for months and years
fields.cellHeight: double? - 32 for days, 40 for months and years
fields.gap: double? - cell and row gap; null = 4
fields.weekdayTextStyle: TextStyle? - weekday header; its colour is muted
fields.cellTextStyle: TextStyle? - cell label; its colour is ignored

accessibility.keyboard: one tab stop per grid (roving tabindex): ArrowLeft/Right a day and wrapping at the row edge, ArrowUp/Down a week, Home/End the ends of the week, PageUp/PageDown a month, Shift plus those a year, Enter/Space select; a disabled cell is skipped by every move and an arrow off the edge leaves the focus put
accessibility.onViewChanged: reported when a page or year move leaves the shown month, carrying the focused day across
accessibility.semantics: each cell is a button node labelled with the full localized date, marked enabled and selected; the painted day number is ExcludeSemantics-wrapped so a screen reader hears the date once
accessibility.focusRing: the focused cell alone is wrapped in FocusOutline, so the ring token paints exactly one ring

sizes.weekdayHeader: 32 wide, the same box as a day cell

notes: `DatePickerDialog` (501 LOC in `_date_picker_dialog_state.dart` plus 99 in `date_picker_dialog.dart`) is NOT migrated: it needs the popover/overlay stack batch B13 owns, and shipping half of it would leave a dialog with no anchor. Batch B13 builds `date_picker` on this component.

`CalendarView`, `CalendarValue` and the three value classes moved to `primitives/date_math.dart`, the batch's named primitive: `date_picker` (B13) and `object_input` (B21) read the same values, so they are data, not component API.

The old `CalendarGridData` re-implemented month arithmetic and always started the grid on a Monday; the port uses the `monthGrid` primitive, so `firstDayOfWeek` is now a parameter and a Sunday-first locale is one argument away.

The old grid wrote `prevMonthLastDay.add(Duration(days: i))` across a DST boundary, which lands on the same day twice in half the world; `monthGrid` builds every cell from `DateTime(y, m, d + i)` instead.

`CalendarItemType` had ten cases for six visual rows (four of them `*RangeSelectedShort` variants no caller ever set) and a 341-line switch; the port has one cell painter driven by `CalendarValueLookup` plus `today`.
`isDateEnabled` and `stateBuilder` were two knobs for one job (`stateBuilder` won); only `stateBuilder` is kept.
`CalendarGridItem.isToday` called `DateTime.now()` from inside the widget, so a grid could not be rendered for any other day; `Calendar.now` is injected instead.
`MonthCalendar` and `YearCalendar` are private now: they were reachable only through `DatePickerDialog`, and the month/year grids are one `viewType` away.

`Clickable` is deliberately not used per cell: it owns a *traversable* focus node per cell, so a 35-cell day grid would be 35 tab stops. The focus lives on the grid instead, and the ring is drawn by the cell from the `ring` token.
`rangeTrackColor` was dropped: the port paints no band behind a range, so the row was dead. `rangeBackground` covers start, end and in-between cells.

`CalendarTheme.copyWith` and `lerp` were dropped as dead code (nothing in the registry calls either, and the calendar has no animated theme change); `==`/`hashCode` read one field list so a new row cannot drift out of them.
